messages:
Maya: Hey team — spotted repeated tail-latency spikes on euz1-dedicated-pool-7 starting ~09:06 UTC, correlated w/ tenant:mlprep-batch. p95 token latency jumped ~3x.
Ravi: saw that, metrics show NVLink TX errors + NIC queue spikes. dumping a sample from node-42 logs:
```
RUNTIME: gpu0 nvlink: tx_err=42, nic_queue=99%
```
Dana: is this noisy-neighbor or thermal?
Maya: thermal looks fine; temps stable. kernel dmesg shows packet drops and TCP retransmits, so egress is suspect.
Keven: FYI routing fallback kicked around 09:08 — some requests silently moved to shared-fractional pools. infra cost for that tenant spiked ~\$120 over 3h.
Maya: can we prevent auto-fallback to shared when the root cause appears to be NIC/egress saturation? fallback is masking the problem.
Ravi: proposal: add a per-pool flag `no_fallback_on_egress_saturation` and emit a `fallback_cost_shift` metric so finance can see diverted spend.
Dana: +1. Right now the ledger attributes cost to the receiver pool which hides who generated the load. We need attribution.
Maya: quick mitigation: soft-quarantine tenant mlprep-batch (cap concurrency & backoff). I pushed a canary command: 
`/ops limit-tenant mlprep-batch --concurrency 10 --backoff 30s --reason \"egress_saturation\"`
deploy-bot: command accepted. policy applied to mlprep-batch on euz1-dedicated-pool-7.
Keven: finance asked if we can tag diverted requests with `billing.asset=dedicated-pool-7` so the cost shows up under the original pool. Router currently strips that tag on reroute.
Ravi: small router change could preserve `original_pool` in headers. risky but bounded. alternative: enrich the admission/log pipeline with `original_pool` field and retro-attribute via logs.
Dana: ops needs this in prod this week if possible. can we do a fast path?
Ravi: I'll open a PR to add a router flag and the `fallback_cost_shift` metric. CI is queued; code review ETA 3h.
Maya: also want an alert: trigger when `fallback_rate > 1%` AND `egress_util > 80%` for > 5m. today alerts fire on either dimension alone and generate noise.
Keven: add a cost dimension too: `cost_rate > $50/hr` as a condition. finance prefers noise-reduced alerts.
Dana: can Console show a contextual suggestion when this alert fires? e.g., `Consider NIC shaping or migrate tenant to a larger dedicated slice`. That would speed ops response.
Maya: will draft the Console copy and post it in #docs-review later today.
Ravi: PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/router/pull/912 (draft).
Keven: finance wants retro accounting for the 3h window (09:06–12:06). Ops: export request_ids for that window so ledger can re-run attribution.
Maya: exported request list to s3: s3://ops-exports/mlprep-burst-3062004321.csv (contains request_id, original_pool, reroute_target, latency).
Dana: nice. if spikes repeat we should schedule a brief postmortem and decide whether to default `no_fallback_on_egress_saturation` for Dedicated pools.
Keven: agreed. also check whether dedicated-pool-7 needs NIC firmware bump; cross-ref ticket in hw-ops.
Maya: opened hw ticket: HWOPS-7892 (nvlink/nic firmware audit).
Ravi: will add the alert + fallback metric to the monitoring dashboard.
Maya: thanks — keeping this thread as the single source for ops/finance action items.
Keven: thx all :thumbsup:
